newsitem.title: USA: LA county rejects PSA request for yield burn data.
newsitem.headline: LA county rejects PSA request for yield burn data.

text.p: Lawyers for a Los Angeles County authority on Thursday formerly rejected a request by municipal bond dealers for background data on a controversial study commissioned by the county on "yield burning."

Phillips & Cohen, lawyers for the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transporation Authority, said in a two-page letter to PSA The Bond Market Trade Association that it would supply the data only if bond dealers agreed to supply the county with detailed pricing documents that their firms used to price escrow securities.

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been shaken by allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond financing transactions, a practice dubbed yield burning.

The Los Angeles County authority, which filed a $14 million lawsuit against Lazard Freres & Co in April 1996 over alleged yield burning, charged in a 43-page study in December that Wall Street firms made roughly $1 billion since 1990 in illegal profits from yield burning overcharges.

PSA officials shot back with charges that the authority's study is deeply flawed. They asked Phillips & Cohen on February 10 to supply the transaction-by-transaction data that the study's authors used to reach their conclusions. PSA said it wants independent experts to review the data.
But Phillips & Cohen's said in this week's letter, released on Thursday, that an outside review is unnecessary.
The firm said it already has submitted the data to independent experts -- the Internal Revenue Service and enforcement officials at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The lawfirm said it is "ironic" that PSA wants more study data when Lazard Frere refuses to turn over background pricing documents in connection with L.A. county's yield burning lawsuit.
Phillips & Cohen pointed in its letter, which is addressed to PSA vice president George Brakatselos, to testimony at a January 15 IRS hearing on yield burning by Brakatselos.

Brakatselos said that PSA member firms are required to keep records that would show the "amounts, prices, (and) time of execution," at which they resold a security, the lawfirm said. Those records would show the markup, the lawfirm said.

PSA's vice president then added that, "If I were a dealer and an issuer came to me and I did an escrow transaction with that issuer ... I would make sure he had all the information to satisfy him or herself that those securities were sold ... at fair market value," according to the lawfirm's letter.
Phillips & Cohen said in the letter released on Thursday that it would make study background data available to PSA if PSA would "make a wider range of data available."
